HomeEssentials Retail - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Retail Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Retail's results for the Q3. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Stores Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Alex Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Retail's performance for the Q3. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover eight key aspects of our performance. First, our financial outlook commentary, which positions us strongly amid retail headwinds. Second, labor costs and store payroll leverage, where we've achieved meaningful improvements. Third, comp sales guidance for next quarter and the year ahead. Fourth, supply chain efficiency improvements that drove significant savings. Fifth, store remodel and renovation plans accelerating our store fleet transformation. Sixth, key assumptions underlying our guidance. Seventh, earnings guidance for the upcoming periods. Eighth, our inventory turnover ratio, reflecting optimized working capital.

These efforts underscore our confidence in navigating the current environment and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.42 billion, a 3.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.1%, primarily driven by lower markdowns, favorable product mix from private labels, and supply chain cost reductions. Operating expenses were $685 million, representing 28.3% of revenue. Net income was $210 million, or $0.95 per share. We generated $360 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently well-controlled at around 52 days outstanding, supporting faster turns.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

To give you more color on these results and our path forward, let me dive deeper into those key aspects Mike highlighted, starting with our financial outlook for the remainder of fiscal 2023 and into 2024. This guidance reflects our disciplined execution in a dynamic retail environment, where brick-and-mortar faces headwinds from inflation, high interest rates, and cautious spending, especially among middle-income households. Yet, our omnichannel approach, optimized stores, and data-driven inventory management set us apart from peers like Macy's and Kohl's, who've posted 4-6% comp declines year-to-date.

For Q4 fiscal 2023, we expect consolidated net sales of $2.45 billion to $2.55 billion, flat to +2% year-over-year. This includes comparable sales growth of 0.5% to 2.5%, fueled by holiday promotions and our Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store program, now 28% of digital orders, up from 22% last year. Digital sales penetration should be 22-24% of total, thanks to our app personalization via Adobe Commerce and Salesforce.

Gross margin is set to expand 20-50 basis points to 38.0-38.3%, from fewer markdowns via AI pricing that cut clearance by 15% year-to-date, stabilized ocean freight at $2,500 per FEU, and mix shifts to higher-margin private labels like Essentials Home, up 12% in Q3. Adjusted SG&A as a percent of sales at 28.5-29.0%, improving 10 basis points sequentially as wage inflation eases to 3.5% for associates, freeing funds for loyalty enhancements. Operating income guided to $285-315 million, adjusted diluted EPS $0.85 to $0.95, with a 24.5% tax rate and 220 million shares.

Capex for the year: $175-200 million, targeting 25 remodels of 120,000 sq ft supercenters, five new stores in Sunbelt areas like Phoenix and Dallas-Fort Worth, and $40 million in supply chain automation like AS/RS at Atlanta and Riverside DCs.

For full-year fiscal 2024, net sales growth of 2.5-4.0%, comps 1.5-3.5%, assuming consumer recovery with 1-2% real disposable income growth per Fed projections. Tailwinds from Store of the Future with RFID in 40% of 1,200 stores by year-end, cutting out-of-stocks 30% like Home Depot, and DoorDash integration for 15% same-day urban penetration. Southeast and Southwest comps over 4% from migration and homeownership; Northeast urban flat to -1% from remote work; Canadian 50 stores +3% with Loblaws lockers.

Gross margins 38.2-38.7%, +50-75 bps from vendor scorecards saving 8% costs and less promo as inflation hits 2-3%. SG&A 28.0-28.3% with 25 bps leverage, offset by $25 million digital marketing. Adjusted EBITDA $1.1-1.2 billion, up 5-10%; free cash flow $650-750 million post-capex, funding $300 million repurchases and 12% dividend hike to $1.20, net debt/EBITDA under 2.0x.

Strategically, traffic-first moves like geo-fencing ads upping walk-ins 7%, Endless Aisle for 20% SKUs via drop-ship, targeting 5.2x inventory turns vs. 4.8x this year. Piloting EV chargers at 100 stores for 15% suburban EV growth. Risks: Asia tariffs (25% COGS), labor shortages above 4% unemployment, weak holiday sentiment; stress-tested for 1-2% comp miss with $1.2 billion liquidity.

This outlook highlights our resilience for market share gains.

Building on that, let's discuss labor costs and store payroll leverage, a major profitability driver where store payroll is our largest controllable SG&A expense at 15-20% of sales industry-wide. For HomeEssentials Retail's 1,200 stores selling kitchen appliances to seasonal decor, leverage comes from comps outpacing labor hours and wages, expanding store margins.

In Q3, store labor was 18.2% of net sales, down 130 bps from 19.5% last year and 40 bps from Q2, with payroll dollars up just 2.1% to $285 million versus 5.8% comp growth—delivering 60 bps store EBITDA expansion. FTEs flat at 42,000 post last year's hiring.

This stems from optimized scheduling with Kronos AI upgrade and demand-sensing for hourly traffic via POS, weather, events—labor hours per $1,000 sales down 4.2% to 12.8, best in three years; superstores at 11.2 vs. 13.1.

Productivity tech: self-checkout at 85% (from 72%), cutting cashiers 15%; handheld scanners slash BOPIS pick times 22%—BOPIS now 18% of store sales, 30% more efficient. RFID pilot in 50 East Coast stores for 5-7% stocking savings.

Wages up 4.5% to $18.67, matching Target/Walmart, turnover down to 28% from 35% via cross-training (65% multi-skilled), Essentials Flex PTO, mental health days.

Sunbelt (420 stores): 17.1% labor on 7.2% comps from migration, outdoor categories. Northeast (280 stores): 19.4% from union premiums, 3.1% comps. Midwest: 18.0% on appliance value.

This moats us vs. Amazon's rising fulfillment; Q4 labor 17.8-18.3% on 4-6% comps, full-year down 100-120 bps. Risks: minimum wage hikes, but tech and 45,000 sq ft footprint protect us. This drove 25% of 110 bps gross margin expansion, targeting 6-8% EBITDA long-term.

Next, on comp sales guidance for Q4 and full year. Comps are our North Star for 92% physical sales from 1,200 stores. Momentum from ValueMax EDLP and remodels laps last year's peak inflation.

Q4 comps +3.0% to +4.0%: flat to +1% traffic, +2.5-3.5% basket; AUR +1-2% with controlled markdowns, private labels 28% grocery sales +450 bps margin in Q3.

Essentials (grocery/HBA/pharmacy) +4-5% from fresh produce, Instacart BOPIS up 15%. GM/apparel +1-2% trading to RetailMax Home/ActiveEdge vs. Amazon/Shein. Hardlines flat +0.5-1.5% holiday decor/appliances, soft housing.

Sunbelt +5-6% on +12% traffic, next-gen 50k sq ft stores +800 bps. Northeast/Midwest +1-2% weather/unemployment. Canada/Mexico +2.5% local currency.

Full-year comps raised to +2.8-3.3% from +2.0-2.8%, Q3 +3.2%, lean holiday inventory 8.5 weeks vs. 10. Q1 FY25 +2-3% sans tariffs. Gross margin +40-60 bps from shrink -25 bps RFID 60% fleet, Memphis DC -15% freight.

Omnichannel: Storefulfillment 85% stores +22% digital attribution. Loyalty 65M households +18%, +1.2x spend, 30% comp traffic. Dynamic pricing pilot +50 bps AUR.

Macro caution: sentiment 110 vulnerable to rates; port risks, election. But +110 bps share gains vs. Walmart/Costco. $1.2B capex 150 remodels/20 new builds.

Turning to supply chain efficiency improvements, a multi-year transformation boosting Q3 gross margins 220 bps to 32.8%, 120 bps from supply chain cuts. End-to-end costs 8.2% of sales, -14.7% YoY. Turnover 7.2x from 5.6x, DIO 51 from 65 days, freeing $450M capital, minimizing stockouts.

$285M invested since 2021 Supply Chain Modernization, 400% three-year ROI.

AI demand sensing with Blue Yonder across 18 DCs: 94% SKU accuracy from POS/weather/econ data, safety stock -22%, in-stock 97.5% from 93%.

Automation: 1.2M sq ft DFW mega-DC AutoStore robots 1,200 picks/hour/operator, throughput +35%, labor +28%. Five urban MFCs (Chicago/LA/Atlanta) AMRs for 99% BOPIS, OTIF 98.2% from 91%, aiding 4.2% comps.

Sourcing: 42% North American hardlines from 28%, multi-year VMI with P&G/Stanley Black & Decker -18% freight, lead times 28 from 45 days.

Midwest/Southeast: cycle <24 hrs, cost/case -16%. West Coast pivoted air/rail vs. port dwell, +2% overrun. Canada Buffalo DC -11% duties/transit.

This builds moat for experiential categories; traffic +3.1%, conversion +1.5 pts. FY24 $75M capex two MFCs/blockchain private labels, 10-12% more leverage, 5-7% comps, 150-200 bps margins.

On store remodel and renovation plans, our highest-ROI initiative transforming 1,200 stores into omnichannel hubs like Target's playbook. Past three years, 320 remodels at $1.2M each, high-volume underperformers: +17% comps year 1, dwell +22%, conversion +8 pts, 2.4-year payback, +250 bps EBITDA vs. NRF 10-15%.

Next three years $650M capex, 45% of $1.4B total: FY24 175 remodels/100 renovations ($1.4M/$450k), prioritized by ROI/demographics/BOPIS. FY25/26 225/year, 20% smaller footprints from 80k sq ft.

Design: open zoning shop-in-shops vignettes like IKEA/Best Buy; modular sustainable fixtures -12% sq ft/SKU, impulse boost.

SmartStore Suite: RFID 99% accuracy -30% OOS; AI signage/kiosks NCR/Intel +14% add-ons; mobile POS/AR mirrors/frictionless 10 lanes/store; BOPIS/curbside 25% sales.

Sustainability: LED -40% energy, low-GWP HVAC, recycled floors; $15-20M IRA credits, appeals to 65% ESG shoppers, 42% GenZ/Millennials.

Sunbelt 60 stores outdoor expansions +20% comps growth; urban smaller + pop-ups vs. TJX; rural EV chargers +30% dwell; Canada 15 bilingual/cold.

Ties to Retail Reimagined: stores 55% sales from 48%; 40% FY25 5-7% comps. Atlanta/Denver/Orlando pilots +21%; early FY24 45 stores +16% vs. 12-18% expect. Essential for $5.5T retail, 80% discovery physical.

Now, key assumptions underlying FY25 guidance: $14.8-15.2B revenue +2-5%, comps flat-+3%, op margin +20-50 bps to 5.5-6.0%, EPS $2.45-2.65. Brick traffic 95% pre-pandemic, e-com 18%.

Macro: GDP 1.8-2.2%, confidence 100-110, CPI 2.5-3.0%, unemployment 4.1-4.3%, wages 3.5%. Apparel +1% NPD, home +2.5% 3.5M home sales.

Sunbelt +4-6% traffic +8%; Midwest flat-+2%; Northeast +3-5% tourism; int'l +1% hedged FX.

Comps: +1% traffic, -2% ASP promo, +1% units AI; sq ft +0.5% 25 new small/15 closures; omni 55% digital.

Gross +25-75 bps to 38.0-38.5%: pricing 50bps EDLP/markdown 22%, RFID 60% shrink 1.3% -$45M, flat freight, private labels 28% +25bps.

SG&A -10bps 32.5%: labor 3.0% Kronos OT -18%, ZBB $20M savings. Capex $450-500M 75% remodels/20% supply chain DFW expansion -25% time.

Brick-to-Click: $100M MFCs 50 stores +20% delivery; experiential +5% comps. Tariffs 10% mitigated 80%.

Sensitivities: -100bps comps -$0.15 EPS; repurchase $300M 2M shares. Conservative vs. peers.

Finally, earnings guidance for Q4 and FY2025. Q3 beat with +4.2% comps, $1.18 EPS. Q4 sales $2.55-2.65B +4-7%, comps 3-5%, EPS $1.45-1.55 +8%. Grocery strength, MaxDeals +12% digital.

Gross 38.2-38.7% +50-100bps RFID 85%, private 28%, DFW DC -15% freight, tariff caution.

SG&A 22.8-23.2% flat, Workforce.com scheduling, wages 3.5%, retention bonuses.

FY25 sales $10.8-11.0B +4.5-5.5%, EPS $4.65-4.85 raised, comps 3.5-4.5% H2 accel. $300M repurchase +$150M Q4.

Southeast/Midwest 5-6%, 15 Express stores; West 1-3%. Canada/Mexico 4% comps Chedraui. BOPIS 22% +30% Swisslog pilots. Loyalty 18M +11% 2.5x basket. Capex $450-500M 60% supply/25% remodels.

Lean 10.5 weeks inventory, vs. Walmart edge private 35% margins.

And wrapping with inventory turnover ratio: FY23 4.9x from 4.3x, best since 2019; Q4 7.2x +12%. COGS $7.8B +5%, avg inventory $1.59B -2%, -80bps carrying $25M savings.

Hardlines 5.8x Right-Stock; softlines 3.9x VMI 40% +22% accuracy; consumables 12.4x EDLP.

Northeast 5.4x BOPIS 28%; Southeast 4.2x hurricanes countered MFCs; West 5.1x sustainable demand.

Drivers: AI Oracle/Google 92% accuracy -18% OOS/-25% over; RFID 85% apparel -30% labor/shrink 1.1%; ship-from-store 35% e-com; OTIF 95% tied payments.

FY24 guide 5.1-5.4x, VMI 60%, dynamic AI 200 stores.

These metrics position us strongly.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Ramirez, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Emily Carter to discuss store operations, Raj Patel to discuss marketing initiatives, and Alex Kim to talk about technology advancements.

David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our Essentials Home line, which has seen strong uptake with 12% growth and higher margins, contributing to mix shifts. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in private labels.

Emily Carter, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented expanded BOPIS zones and RFID pilots, and are seeing positive results in traffic and conversion.

Raj Patel, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Emily. Our new marketing campaign, Home Refresh, has increased brand awareness by 18% through geo-fencing and loyalty personalization.

Alex Kim, Chief Technology Officer:
Thank you, Raj. We have invested in AI-powered demand sensing and workforce management platforms, which have improved our forecasting accuracy and scheduling efficiency.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a pressure, but our value pricing and private labels have helped, with comps holding strong. Our guidance assumes CPI cooling to 2-3%, supporting basket growth as real wages recover—we're gaining share in essentials where consumers prioritize value.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Maria. As detailed, Q4 comps at 3-4%, accelerating full-year to 2.8-3.3%, with Sunbelt leading on traffic from new stores and remodels. We're conservative on macro but see leverage from omnichannel and lean inventory.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Wilson (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Tom. Our AI forecasting, DFW mega-DC automation, and MFCs have boosted OTIF to 98%, turnover to 7.2x in Q4, and cut costs 14.7%—key to 120 bps margin help and supporting BOPIS growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Anna Lee (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Anna. Loyalty now at 65 million households, driving 1.2x spend and 30% comp traffic—up 18% YoY. Enhancements like personalization are embedded in our guidance for basket uplift.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel (Deutsche Bank):
Thanks. On store remodels, what's the expected ROI timeline?

Emily Carter, Chief Stores Officer:
Hi Chris. Our remodels deliver 2.4-year payback on average, with pilots at 16-21% comp lifts. FY24's 175 will fuel 40% of comp guidance, focusing high-ROI Sunbelt and urban prototypes.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] That concludes our Q&A. Thank you.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
